misconceptions.error: Mixes county government with national government (puts the President and MPs in the county).

example.question: Who is in the county executive?
example.correct_answer: The Governor

misconceptions.cause: The child hears the names on the news and puts them all together.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The President" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Make two columns: national and county, and place each leader.
misconceptions.feedback: The county executive has the Governor, Deputy Governor and executive committee. The President belongs to the national government.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Puts the Governor in the county assembly or the MCAs in the executive.

example.question: Which one is a member of the county assembly?
example.correct_answer: A Member of the County Assembly (MCA)

misconceptions.cause: The child does not tell the two parts apart.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The Governor" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Draw two boxes: executive, assembly; place each person.
misconceptions.feedback: The assembly is made of the MCAs and the Speaker. The Governor heads the executive.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the Governor makes the county laws.

example.question: Who makes the county laws?
example.correct_answer: The county assembly

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks the head makes all rules.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The Governor" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Ask: who makes the rules at school and who sees they are followed?
misconceptions.feedback: The assembly makes county laws. The Governor sees that they are carried out.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the Governor is the head of the whole country.

example.question: The Governor is head of which?
example.correct_answer: The county

misconceptions.cause: The child has the Governor and the President confused.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The whole country" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Place the Governor and the President on a map of Kenya: which area does each lead?
misconceptions.feedback: The Governor leads the county. The President leads the whole country.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the MCA carries out county work, building roads and running hospitals himself.

example.question: What does an MCA do?
example.correct_answer: Makes county laws and approves the budget

misconceptions.cause: The child links leaders with doing the work.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Builds the roads himself" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Ask who writes the plan and who builds the road.
misconceptions.feedback: The MCA makes county laws, approves the budget and checks the executive. The county executive carries out the work.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks an MCA speaks for the whole country or the whole county.

example.question: Whom does an MCA represent?
example.correct_answer: The people of his or her ward

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes up an MCA and an MP.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The whole country" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Mark a ward on a sketch and name the MCA.
misconceptions.feedback: An MCA is elected by a ward and speaks for its people. Members of Parliament sit in the National Assembly.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the county government is one person, the Governor.

example.question: Is the county government only the Governor?
example.wrong_answer: Yes, the Governor is the county government
example.correct_answer: No: it is the county executive and the county assembly

misconceptions.cause: The Governor is the face of the county on news and posters.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Yes, the Governor is the county government" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Draw the two boxes and fill them with all the people in each.
misconceptions.feedback: The county government has two parts: the executive, led by the Governor, and the county assembly.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CBC Social Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Puts the Speaker of the County Assembly in the county executive.

example.question: Is the Speaker of the County Assembly part of the county executive?
example.correct_answer: No, the Speaker leads the meetings of the county assembly

misconceptions.cause: Both sound like senior offices, so the child puts them together.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Yes, with the Governor" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Put the Speaker's card in the assembly box and say what the Speaker does there.
misconceptions.feedback: The Speaker belongs to the county assembly and chairs its meetings.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CBC Social Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks a Governor stays in office for life.

example.question: How long is a Governor's term?
example.correct_answer: Five years, then there is an election

misconceptions.cause: The child does not connect leaders with terms and elections.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "For life" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Show the general election cycle: every five years.
misconceptions.feedback: A Governor is elected for five years at a time.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CBC Social Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the President appoints the Governor.

example.question: Who chooses the Governor of a county?
example.correct_answer: The voters of the county, in an election

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks every senior office is filled by the President.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The President" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Ask who votes in the county at a general election.
misconceptions.feedback: The people of the county elect their Governor.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CBC Social Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks MCAs are chosen by the Governor.

example.question: Who chooses the Member of the County Assembly for a ward?
example.correct_answer: The voters of the ward

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks the Governor, as county head, picks everyone below.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The Governor" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Name what is on the ballot at a general election, including the MCA.
misconceptions.feedback: The people of each ward elect their MCA.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CBC Social Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the Governor alone decides how the county spends money, with no role for the assembly.

example.question: Who approves the county budget?
example.correct_answer: The county assembly, made up of MCAs

misconceptions.cause: The child sees the Governor as the one who spends.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The Governor alone" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Act a budget: the executive proposes, the MCAs debate and vote.
misconceptions.feedback: The county assembly approves the budget. The executive then spends it.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CBC Social Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.
